subject: QBR prep: SLO heatmap + incident impact and exec talking points
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: SLO heatmap + incident impact and exec talking points

Team —

Attached is a concise package I put together for QBR prep: a one-page incident timeline (PDF), the Q2 SLO heatmap (CSV), and a draft customer comms doc. High-level summary up front so we can use the slide deck for execs tomorrow: 

- What happened: transient KV cache corruption on 2026-06-08 (02:14–02:46 UTC) that caused increased tail latency and intermittent token drops for a subset of customers on Dedicated clusters running models > 30k context.
- Impact: 42 customer incidents opened, 3 customers logged SLA exceptions (totaling ~18 minutes of aggregated SLA exposure across routed requests), peak error rate 6% for affected nodes.
- Root cause (current): a race condition in the cache eviction path interacting with an emergent kernel scheduling change. Patch pushed 06-09 15:00 UTC; rollforward validated 06-09 18:30 UTC.
- Business impact: minimal revenue loss but reputational risk for two high-touch accounts (NimbusAI, Acme Corp). We should propose a small goodwill credit (suggested $6k) and proactive postmortem with SRE- and CS-led outreach.

Action items for QBR slides / exec talking points (short bullets we can read out):
1) What we measured: SLO breach window, affected capacity, rough customer exposure minutes (see CSV).
2) What we fixed: immediate kernel rollback and targeted eviction-path patch; mitigations: expanded preforked eviction workers to reduce contention; longer-term: kernel scheduler hardening and additional e2e tests.
3) What we will do: automated detection for eviction anomalies (owner: SRE — Rishi), expanded chaos tests for long-context models (owner: Applied ML — Vivek), and playbook updates for Dedicated failover (owner: Product Ops — Laura).
4) Customer handling: draft outreach + offer credit (owner: CS — Laura).

Please review the attached timeline and heatmap. I want two short bullets per person for the QBR slide deck: what we did, and what we're committing to for the quarter. Can each of you reply with your two bullets by EOD Friday?

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-06-10_incident-timeline.pdf, slo-heatmap-q2.csv, customer-comm-draft.md

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: SLO heatmap + incident impact and exec talking points

Marcus —

Thanks for the crisp summary. A couple quick items I want called out for the exec notes: 

- Decision made during the incident: rollback to kernel v5.9.3 for affected fleets at 02:58 UTC. That rollback bought us time while the eviction fix was prepared. We should note rollback as a deliberate mitigation to highlight our ability to trade forward progress for stability.
- Short-term commitment: put a hard flag on any future kernel scheduler rollout to run as canary for 72h with strict observability gates. (one-liner for slide)
- Financial ask: approve the proposed $6k credit for NimbusAI and Acme as part of the QBR remedial table. I'll sponsor the ask to finance.

Two bullets for the slide (as requested):
- We restored stability via kernel rollback + eviction patch; immediate mitigation validated within 3 hours.
- Commit to canary gating for kernel rollouts + automated eviction anomaly detection (owners: Infra + SRE).

I'll sync with Rishi offline on the anomaly detection timeline.

— Vivek

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: SLO heatmap + incident impact and exec talking points

Folks —

Thanks Marcus, this is clear. A few practical notes for the QBR slide and next steps on comms: 

- Customer comms: I've updated the draft (attached) to include timeline, impact, and remediation steps. I recommend a two-paragraph proactive email to NimbusAI with the offer and a proposed follow-up meeting. CS lead is Priya; she will draft the personalized outreach.
- Credit: agree on the $6k total; suggest splitting as $3k for NimbusAI, $2k for Acme Corp, $1k pool for minor customers. Need Finance approval; I can own the request and get signoff before QBR.
- QBR slide ask: add a single slide with the 'SLO heatmap' visual and a callout box with the two exec bullets from Vivek + Marcus. Keep it to one slide, please.

Two bullets for deck: 
- Immediate: rollback + targeted eviction patch restored service; validated within 3 hours. (Owner: Infra + SRE)
- Commitment: targeted canary gates and automated eviction anomaly alerts; CS will proactively contact affected accounts with offer. (Owner: Product Ops + CS)

I'll circulate the comms note to Priya and copy you both once she personalizes.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Looping back with the two bullets and a tentative timeline: 

- Two-slide commitment: (1) Incident summary + SLO heatmap; (2) Action plan & owners (Rishi — Eviction anomaly detector: prototype by end of Q3; Vivek — chaos tests for >30k context models: roadmap in two weeks).
- Risk mitigation timeline: prototype anomaly detector (Q3 end), low-latency fallback (Q4), updated rollouts gating (effective immediately for all kernel changes).

Also: quick note on metrics — I'm attaching an excerpt of the error-rate distribution we discussed; it shows the tail spike clearly between 02:20–02:46 UTC. We'll include that chart as backup in the QBR appendix.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of SRE
Redwood Inference
